name: Croatia
summary_text: Croatia is broadly workable with a cleaner documented traveler-axis profile than its Balkan neighbours: no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, police-brutality case, or foreign-trans-detention case surfaced in research. The Dalmatian coast's international-tourism culture (Dubrovnik, Hvar, Split) is broadly open, and Zagreb has the Balkans' most established gay scene. The framework is weaker than Western Europe's: legal gender recognition (available since 2015) is partial and not self-ID (it covers only some documents), there is no marriage equality (a 2013 constitutional ban), and an anti-gender movement is active. A 2024 prosecution of a host who refused to accommodate a gay couple shows enforcement works, and the President was formally criticised for outing a minister. The Catholic-conservative climate is more marked outside the main tourist areas. Croatia is in the EU and Schengen, so border friction for most travellers is low.

sources.claim_summary: Zagreb Pride documentation report (2018) on Croatia's implementation of CoE Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5: hate-crime legislation and under-reporting of homophobic/transphobic crimes, hate speech case studies, freedom of assembly, legal gender recognition, same-sex partnership recognition, employment discrimination, and compiled hate-crime data with case studies.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Croatia: a Zadar prosecutor charged a man for refusing a gay couple's accommodation booking (2018 incident); anti-gender disinformation escalating - a Croatian Parliament session on 'Gender Ideology' featured speakers spreading misinformation with no LGBTI organisations invited; the first Pula Pride march faced disruption the day before.

sources.title: Search Of Persons – Specific Characteristics Of Conducting Searches Of Transgender, Trans, And Gender Non-Conforming Persons
sources.claim_summary: Croatian legal journal article (2026, in Croatian) by Nenad Igrec: 'Search of Persons - Specific Characteristics of Conducting Searches of Transgender, Trans, and Gender Non-Conforming Persons' - academic analysis of how personal searches should be conducted for trans and gender-nonconforming people under Croatian law.

sources.title: Croatia - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Practices report for Croatia (archived): official assessment including treatment of LGBTI persons.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Croatia - Wikipedia
sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview: same-sex activity legal since 1977; life partnership since 2014; gender identity and expression sections; hate-crime legislation; police cooperation; Pride events including Zagreb, Split, Osijek, Karlovac, Pula and the Balkans Trans Inter March; LGBT tourism.

sources.title: LGBTQIA+ Travel in Croatia | Intrepid Travel US
sources.claim_summary: Intrepid Travel country guide: Croatia 'widely accepts' LGBTQIA+ travellers — legal since 1977, with recent life-partnership and protection laws — but PDA may draw unwelcome responses outside big cities and gay venues are virtually non-existent outside Zagreb.

European Commission legal experts' country report on non-discrimination in Croatia (2024, reporting period 2023): transposition and implementation of the EU equality directives, including SOGI grounds.

sources.title: Split dobio LGBT Centar, sve spremno za Povorku ponosa - CroL
sources.claim_summary: CroL (May 2014, in Croatian): Split got an LGBT Centre - the second in Croatia and first in Dalmatia; the 4th Split Pride (7 June 2014) announced with the slogan 'Potpuna ravnopravnost' (Full equality), repeated from the previous year to signal LGBT people's unequal position in Croatia.

sources.title: Predstavljen LGBTIQ+ centar Druga Rijeka - CroL
sources.claim_summary: CroL (Oct 2014, in Croatian): the LGBTIQ+ centre Druga Rijeka was presented in Rijeka - founded from the local community's need for more active LGBTIQ+ development in Primorsko-goranska county, networking with national and international organisations.
